bullets.title: META surges 32.7% in September on Muse AI agent launch—best month since 2013
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts flagged META's massive rally: Hedgeye noted +32.7% for the month (best since 2013), driven entirely by the Muse AI agent launch. Options volume hit 1.8M contracts, highest since Oct '22. Goldman flagged Muse as the most talked-about desk theme, driving shorting of 'Consumer Inertia' basket (GSXUSWCH -2.58%). Shopify (+7.3%) and PYPL/EXPE rose on Muse partnership announcements. Amazon separately blocked Muse from accessing its retail site, flagged as competitive tension.

bullets.title: AMD joins $1T market cap club for first time; INTC +13% on CPU-demand narrative
bullets.body: AMD surpassed $1 trillion market capitalization—its first time—rising ~10% on the day, driven by the narrative that agentic AI workloads require far more CPUs relative to GPUs (3–4 CPUs per GPU for inference vs. 7–8 for training). INTC also surged ~12–13% as analysts noted NVIDIA selected Intel Xeon 6 as the host CPU for DGX Rubin, and TSMC's advanced nodes are fully booked, positioning INTC 18A as a credible alternative foundry. ARM similarly rallied ~14%.

bullets.title: NVDA: forward P/E hits decade-low of 15.75; insider sells $300M; options IV declining
bullets.body: NVDA's forward P/E compressed to 15.75, described as the lowest in over a decade. Board member Mark Stevens sold $300M in shares, described as one of the largest NVDA shareholders. Separately, options surface across 3–18 months is becoming cheaper even as the stock rallies from an ascending triangle breakout, with 76.4% Fibonacci resistance at $2,034. Semis (including NVDA and MU) rose for a sixth consecutive session as Nasdaq hit its first record close since June.

bullets.title: Michael Burry increases shorts on MU, NBIS, PLTR; bearish on semis
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm Michael Burry increased short positions in Micron (MU), Nebius (NBIS), and Palantir (PLTR), with disclosure showing him bearish on iShares Semiconductor ETF. NBIS meanwhile raised H200 pricing by ~19% and H100 pricing ~16.5%, with B300 on-demand pricing at its highest—past hikes corresponded with $20+ stock rallies.

bullets.title: Taiwan August export orders surge 71.4% YoY—beat consensus 63% on ASIC/AI demand
bullets.body: Taiwan's August export orders reached $102.96B, up 71.4% YoY and well above the 63% consensus estimate. Growth was driven by AI-related demand and a surge in custom ASIC chip design orders. Taiwan telcos reported 60–70% YoY iPhone 18 Pro sales growth in the first three days, and TSMC's 2nm chips are now shipping in the iPhone 18 Pro series, Xiaomi, Vivo, and Oppo flagships.

bullets.title: AVGO expects 100% supply-constrained YoY growth; memory LTAs extend to 2031
bullets.body: One analyst noted AVGO expects 100% supply-constrained Y/Y growth for the next two years, while NVDA expects 70% supply-constrained growth next year. Memory long-term agreements extend to 2031, creating a multi-year demand backlog. Silicon wafer prices (12-inch epitaxial) are forecast to rise 15–25% in 2027 as capacity expansion drives demand.

bullets.title: MSFT upgraded to Buy at Stifel, $575 PT; launches AI 'super app' with Copilot discounts
bullets.body: Stifel upgraded Microsoft to Buy with a $575 price target, citing sustainable mid-to-upper-teens revenue growth driven by LLM agnosticism and Azure momentum. Separately, The Information reported Microsoft is boosting Copilot discounts as it launches an AI 'super app.' Microsoft's custom AI chip is on track for mass production in 2027, and the company doubled its Taiwan AI data center plan from 2 to 4 facilities.

bullets.title: AAPL hits $5T market cap; iPhone 18 Pro sees 60–70% YoY sales surge; screenless tracker in dev
bullets.body: Apple's market cap crossed $5 trillion. Taiwan telecom operators reported 60–70% YoY growth for iPhone 18 Pro in the first three days. TSMC's 2nm chips are confirmed in the Pro lineup. Apple is also developing a screenless health/fitness wearable to compete with WHOOP, and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman confirmed John Ternus as incoming CEO.

bullets.title: Agentic AI driving CPU supercycle: AMD, INTC, ARM seen as primary beneficiaries
bullets.body: Multiple accounts called the CPU demand surge the 'agentic supercycle'—Meta's Muse AI agent requires significant CPU resources (CPUs, DRAM, SSDs) and could need 1.58M AMD Ryzen CPUs at 100M users. The ratio of CPUs to GPUs shifts heavily toward CPUs for inference vs. training workloads. GS factor dashboard shows GAI infrastructure as top performer. QCOM also announced partnership with MA on agentic payments infrastructure via Snapdragon devices.

bullets.title: SNDK initiated Buy at Rosenblatt, $2,400 PT; SNDK shows first +1z score in ages
bullets.body: Rosenblatt initiated SNDK coverage with a Buy rating and $2,400 price target, noting management targets mid-to-high-teens revenue growth and ~80% gross margins by FY2028–30. A separate trader noted SNDK hasn't shown a +1 standard deviation score in ages and predicted continued upside through 2027. Bullish sovereign AI deployment thesis also cited for NVDA, MU, SNDK, LITE names.

bullets.title: COHR launches PhotonLink integrated optics platform for AI datacenters at ECOC
bullets.body: Coherent officially launched PhotonLink at ECOC 2026 on September 21—an integrated optics platform for AI datacenters spanning the full optical signal chain from light generation through reception, with CPO support. LITE similarly showcased VCSEL platform for AI optical links with Qualcomm and Corning partners. Evercore upgraded CIEN to Outperform citing 30%+ annual sales growth and $25+ EPS by FY2029.

bullets.title: Macro: Fed hiked 25bps last week; markets now 50/50 on another hike; yields at 4.787%
bullets.body: Markets entered the week pricing in 2 Fed rate cuts at the start of 2026—now pricing at least 1 additional hike after last week's 25bps move. Boston Fed Collins voted for the hike citing persistent inflation and Middle East energy risks. Goolsbee warned restoring price stability 'won't be painless' and won't let supply shocks go unaddressed. 2Y Treasury auction printed 4.787% with 0.2bps tail and weak foreign demand.

bullets.title: Institutional equity allocation hits 57.4%—highest since dot-com; market breadth deteriorating
bullets.body: Institutional investors reached 57.4% equity allocation, described as the highest since the dot-com bubble, raising potential overallocation risk. Despite Nasdaq 100 hitting its first record close since June (+0.8%), market breadth continued to deteriorate—only ~30% of S&P stocks above 50-day MA, 6 consecutive days of more 52-week lows than highs. The S&P rally was described as 'size-led'—equal-weight SPW lagged the cap-weighted index by ~130bps.

bullets.title: AMZN trading at AWS + Anthropic value with zero credit for other assets; Muse blocking adds complexity
bullets.body: One analyst argued AMZN is trading entirely at AWS + Anthropic stake value with no premium for retail, advertising, or other segments. AWS is now the first cloud provider approved for NATO RESTRICTED workloads across all 32 member nations. Amazon also blocked Meta's Muse agent from its retail site, seen as competitive tension in agentic commerce. Trump's July disclosures showed he sold $25M each of AMZN and MSFT.

bullets.title: Oil on 6–7 day losing streak; Brent settles near $100; Iran talks drive volatility
bullets.body: Crude fell 4–5% over the session on US-Iran diplomatic progress and Saudi Arabia restarting Yanbu port loadings. Brent briefly fell below $100 for first time since Sept 9. Iran conditionally offered to open Hormuz within 7 days if US lifts blockade. US also proposed a $5B Gulf energy infrastructure rebuild fund. Strait of Hormuz traffic fell to 2–3 vessels vs. ~125/day pre-conflict average. Diesel hit all-time high of $6.53/gallon, up 76% YoY.

bullets.title: INTC: US Government's $8.9B stake now worth $52B; foundry optimism on 18A and HBM5
bullets.body: The US Government purchased 433.3M Intel shares at $20.47 in August 2025; those shares are now worth $52.2B at ~$120.47. TSMC advanced nodes are described as fully booked, positioning INTC 18A as a pragmatic base die partner for SK Hynix and Micron. A separate report noted Intel is expected to win HBM5 supply contract beginning late 2028. Melius analyst Ben Reitzes published foundry valuation work on INTC with $105.7B net PP&E.

bullets.title: GEV accelerates $200B backlog target to early 2027; guidance seen as conservative
bullets.body: GE Vernova now expects to reach $200B backlog by early 2027, ahead of prior 2027 guidance. Author argues the 20 GW gross new contract additions target is conservative, with GEV likely to exit the year above 125 GW guidance for contracted gas turbines. Data center moratorium wave noted: Texas froze new permits and California passed AI oversight legislation.

bullets.title: NBIS pricing hikes signal GPU pricing power; stock up $20+ on prior hikes
bullets.body: NBIS announced up to 20% price hikes on H200, H100, and B300 on-demand GPU compute—the B300 at its highest price from any vendor. Past NBIS hike announcements drove the stock $20+. Oracle was also cited as raising pricing for 4+ year equipment. One analyst argued NBIS financing model is more sustainable than CRWV and other neocloud peers.

bullets.title: CART bearish: ad revenue concentration poses EBITDA risk; ABNB expands with Instacart
bullets.body: One analyst flagged Instacart (CART) as the most at-risk internet company—ad revenue represents a disproportionate share of both GTV and EBITDA, leaving it exposed to any demand slowdown vs. sector peers. Separately, Airbnb announced expansion of its grocery delivery service with Instacart across US and Canada, enabling app-based pre-stay ordering.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit expected light on major deals; US-China trade truce may extend 3–6 months
bullets.body: US proposed extending the China trade truce by six months; China pushed for a longer extension. The Trump-Xi summit (Sept 23–25) was described as 'light on major deals' with no Chinese CEO delegation expected. Rare earth magnet exports to US fell 21% in August. Bessent confirmed US-China discussions included AI, economics, and tariffs, with a US-China AI meeting in Shenzhen planned in two months.
